title: Operating Systems
description: Can use processes, threads, virtual memory, filesystems and system calls — and can show which isolation or sync choice a failure actually needs.

levels.name: Foundation
levels.description: Can start a parent/child process pair, record the system calls and pids involved, and distinguish a process from a program — under written guidance.

levels.name: Apprentice
levels.description: Can reproduce a race under stress, apply a lock that protects a stated invariant, and write a test that fails when the race returns.

levels.name: Practitioner
levels.description: Can independently map virtual versus resident memory from measurements, run a filesystem experiment that shows write() returning is not durability, and document the cleanup path for a failed child.

levels.name: Journeyman
levels.description: Can diagnose a deadlock from wait relationships, distinguish reserved or virtual pages from resident ones when a symptom looks like a leak, and produce a note another engineer can use to reproduce the bug without a textbook.

levels.name: Mastery Evidence
levels.description: Can review another apprentice's concurrency fix, name a lock that protects no invariant (or an invariant with no lock), and teach when a thread versus a process is the right isolation boundary on an unfamiliar program.
